description:
Send a WhatsApp text message.

Set exactly one recipient: `number`, `group_id`, or `contact_id`.

Writing `@<number>` in the text mentions that person, for example
`@5511999999999`. The platform detects it automatically; there is no
separate mentions argument.

This is also how to answer the message you just received: a normal
message to its sender, as a person does in a chat, with no quote. Quote
(`quoted_message_id`, or `reply_to_message`) only an earlier message that
your answer depends on.

A text message you sent can be corrected later with `edit_text_message`.

Like a person opening the chat, the number first appears online and its
unread messages in that conversation are marked as read, then the
message is sent. Opening the conversation this way is automatic and uses no quota of its own.

Returns the new `message_id` and its initial status. Delivery happens
asynchronously; poll `get_message_status` or watch `list_events` for the
outcome.

contact_id.description: Recipient contact id (`ct_…`), from `list_contacts`. A contact id belongs to one number: an id from one inbox does not address the same person in another. Set exactly one of `number`, `group_id` or `contact_id`.
contact_id.title: Contact Id

group_id.description: Recipient group id (`grp_…`), from `list_groups`. A group id belongs to one number: an id from one inbox does not address the same group in another. Set exactly one of `number`, `group_id` or `contact_id`. Addressing a group needs a plan that includes group messaging: without it the call answers `payment_required: feature_not_available`, and retrying will not change that.
group_id.title: Group Id

idempotency_key.description: Any printable ASCII text you choose, 1 to 255 characters, for example the id of the event you are answering. Reusing it for the same number suppresses a duplicate if you retry. Without it, retrying after a timeout may deliver the message twice, and the recipient sees both.
idempotency_key.title: Idempotency Key

number.description: Recipient phone number in E.164 form, digits only, country code first (e.g. `5511999999999`). Set exactly one of `number`, `group_id` or `contact_id`.
number.title: Number

number_alias.description: Which of the organization's WhatsApp numbers this acts on: `main`, the alias of an extra number, or the number's `id` (`num_…`), which stays the same when the alias is renamed. Call `list_numbers` to see them. Defaults to the main number.
number_alias.title: Number Alias

quoted_message_id.description: Quote an earlier message (`msg_…`) so it appears above yours. Do this only when your text depends on something said a while ago, yours or theirs; do not quote the message you are answering right now, send a normal message instead.
quoted_message_id.title: Quoted Message Id

text.description: The message text, 1 to 4096 characters. Write `@<number>` to mention someone.
text.title: Text

name: send_text
title: Send a text message
